task: Iteration 3 of the great-dirac-w0ytk7 autonomous loop. Iterations 1-2 twice-replicated that the exposure12 quality-champion smoke suite genuinely cannot finish inside decode_timeout_seconds=30 on this hardware/config even after two real fixes (lexer/scanner cache #1173; deadline-swallow fix landed as 30d8dd9). Both prior docs' own next-steps pointed at compiler_ms (build_completion_forest, the Node-bridge grammar-validation round trip) as the actual remaining cost, and decode-compiler-tree-lexer-cache-hero-rerun-20260728.md separately reported compiler_prefill_batches growing 3->17 and 4->33 across its before/after comparison. This session asks the natural next falsifiable question directly motivated by that growth: is the neural prefill-batch width itself (ModelBuildConfig.compiler_prefill_max_states, which chunks the compiler-tree's per-position child-scoring denoiser calls) now a material contributor to wall time, such that bounding it would let the hero/callout/button records finish sooner?
hypothesis: Capping compiler_prefill_max_states to 1 (forcing one ambiguous grammar state per neural prefill batch, i.e. scripts/run_perf_matrix.py's existing C9 arm) reduces latency_ms_p50/p95 and/or changes decode_outcome away from runtime_timeout for the exposure12 champion's 3 isolated smoke records under decode_timeout_seconds=30, relative to the default auto-batched arm (max_states=0, CPU default 4).
why_no_new_decode_machinery: compiler_prefill_max_states and compiler_prefill_token_budget already exist as ModelBuildConfig fields (twotower.py:487-488) and are already swept as a lever pair by scripts/run_perf_matrix.py's C9 (serial, max_states=1) vs C10 (auto, max_states=0) experiments -- no new decode-time code was written. The only gap was CLI/lever plumbing: scripts/evaluate_model.py has no --compiler-prefill-max-states flag and the key was not registered in src/slm_training/flags/levers.py's LEVER_BY_KEY (ruleset_from_mapping rejects unregistered keys), so scripts/evaluate_model.py --flags-json could not reach it. Fixed with a single-line lever registration (default 0, byte-identical to the existing ModelBuildConfig default, so an empty ruleset is unaffected) -- the same tiny, reversible, default-off pattern as every other entry in LEVER_FLAGS.

lever_added.change: Registered compiler_prefill_max_states as a NUMBER lever, default 0 (auto/device-aware, matches ModelBuildConfig.compiler_prefill_max_states's own default), diagnostic-only per its description string.

decision: REJECT the hypothesis. Capping compiler_prefill_max_states to 1 (forcing serial, one-ambiguous-state-per-batch neural prefill scoring, run_perf_matrix.py's existing C9 arm) changes neither decode_outcome (all 6 runs across both arms report runtime_timeout) nor latency_ms_p50 in any consistent or material direction (deltas of -0.14ms, +99.9ms, +199.8ms against a 30000ms wall -- noise-scale, not a trend, and if anything the capped arm is marginally slower on 2 of 3 records). Both arms used the byte-identical cadeb1d3... checkpoint, confirming this is a same-model comparison.
interpretation: This is exactly what the code predicts on inspection, and this run confirms it empirically rather than by argument alone: compiler_ms (the timer wrapping build_completion_forest, the ~97% wall-clock sink identified in decode-compiler-tree-deadline-swallow-finding.md) is recorded in twotower.py around the build_completion_forest call only (line ~10341); compiler_prefill_max_states instead bounds a *separate* denoiser-forward batching loop inside _select_compiler_path (twotower.py ~9797-9847), timed under trie_ms, which both prior docs' isolated-record measurements already showed was negligible (67-72ms total, versus compiler_ms's ~29200ms). Bounding a batch-width knob on a sub-1% cost cannot move a 97%-dominated wall-clock outcome. decode-compiler-tree-lexer-cache-hero-rerun-20260728.md's compiler_prefill_batches 3->17 / 4->33 growth (used to motivate this session's hypothesis) tracks the number of decode-loop iterations x per-iteration prefill chunking, not the compiler_ms sink itself -- it is a correlated symptom of more grammar-forest positions being explored, not a cost driver in its own right.
side_finding_decode_stats_unavailable_fo: Confirms and extends decode-compiler-tree-deadline-fix-applied-rerun-20260728.md's decode_stats_populated=false observation: none of this session's 6 eval runs (all outcome=runtime_timeout post iteration-2's fix) populated metrics['decode_stats'] at all -- the key is entirely absent from the suite JSON, not merely zeroed. Root cause (read, not further modified this session): eval_runner.py's per-chunk timeout handler (line ~1161) does `stats = getattr(exc, 'decode_stats', None)` expecting the propagated TimeoutError to carry a `.decode_stats` attribute, but nothing in the codebase (check_decode_deadline's bare `raise TimeoutError(...)`, nor the SIGALRM handler's `raise TimeoutError(...)`) ever sets that attribute -- grep-confirmed zero matches for `.decode_stats =` anywhere in src/slm_training. This means the fixed-and-honest runtime_timeout classification (iteration 2's genuine win) came at the cost of losing per-record compiler_ms/compiler_prefill_batches/trie_ms telemetry for exactly the records that most need root-cause attribution. This session's REJECT verdict above is therefore based on the only telemetry still available post-fix (latency_ms_p50/p95, decode_outcome), not on a direct before/after compiler_ms comparison -- a materially weaker evidence base than iteration 1's pre-fix isolated-record diagnostic, and worth fixing before the next latency-attribution session.
